message.content: The sea typically looks blue because water absorbs colors at the red end of the spectrum and scatters blue wavelengths. However, its appearance can vary—shallow waters may look turquoise or greenish, while deeper areas can appear darker blue or even black. Factors like algae, sediment, and the angle of sunlight also influence how we perceive its color.
